suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add convention: Servlet display values (badge CSS classes, display names) should be computed consistently — either all in servlets via request attributes, or all in JSP via JSTL. Currently POV status badges are servlet-computed but criteria status badges use inline JSTL c:choose blocks. Recommend documenting a preferred approach.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: PovServlet.java passes badgeClass/statusDisplayName as request attributes for POV status (pov-list-create, pov-detail-edit-delete). detail.jsp uses inline JSTL for criteria status badges. Dead getCriteriaStatusDisplayName/getCriteriaBadgeClass utility methods exist in PovServlet but are unused.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Document the test port allocation strategy explicitly: each servlet integration test class uses a dedicated port in the 8090-8099 range (e.g., TimeEntryServletTest:8098, PovServletTest:8098, CriteriaServletTest:8097, DashboardServletTest:8098). As more test classes are added, this could lead to port collisions if not tracked. Consider documenting which ports are used by which test class.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: DashboardServletTest uses 8098, CriteriaServletTest uses 8097. Multiple test classes share port 8098 but run sequentially via Surefire single-fork mode, so no actual conflict occurs. However, the convention is implicit.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Document the constructor-injection pattern for servlet testability: servlets should have a default no-arg constructor for production (uses production DAOs) and a parameterized constructor accepting DAO instances for testing. This pattern is consistently used across all servlets.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: DashboardServlet, PovServlet, CriteriaServlet, and TimeEntryServlet all follow this pattern. It enables integration testing via embedded Jetty while allowing unit-style DAO mocking if needed.
